event.title: Africa Cup of Nations to Keep Two-Year Cycle Following CAF Decision
event.canonical_title: Africa Cup of Nations to Keep Two-Year Cycle Following CAF Decision
event.summary: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has decided to maintain the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) on a two-year cycle. This decision comes after an earlier announcement that proposed shifting AFCON to a four-year cycle alongside the introduction of a new biennial competition, the Africa Nations League.

revisions.title: Africa Cup of Nations to Keep Biennial Format Following CAF Decision
revisions.summary: The Confederation of African Football has reversed its earlier decision and confirmed that the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) will continue to be held every two years. This decision comes after CAF had initially announced plans to shift AFCON to a four-year cycle alongside the introduction of a new biennial competition, the Africa Nations League.
key_facts: AFCON will maintain its two-year cycle.
CAF had previously announced a shift to a four-year cycle.
The Africa Nations League is a new biennial competition introduced by CAF.
